newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Bogota stock exchange chief to resign.
newsitem.headline: Bogota stock exchange chief to resign.

text.p: The chairman of the Bogota stock exchange, Carlos Caballero, said Thursday he would resign in April from the post he has held since 1994.

"I have asked the directors of the Bogota exchange not to put my name forward for a new period between April 1997 and March 1998. I don't want to carry on because these jobs wear you out and I feel that I have come to the end of my time here," Caballero told Reuters.

Caballero presided over the Bogota exchange at one of the most critical periods in its recent history, marked by price falls and general lethargy. But things are looking up, with Bogota's IBB index up about 27 percent since the start of the year.

He was instrumental in enlisting the aid of the chief prosecutor's office to introduce anti-money laundering regulations into the markets and suspended three brokerages for suspected illegal trading practices last year.
"You end up treading on a lot of people's toes in this job and when you have to suspend firms nobody likes it," Caballero said.
The stock exchange directors are scheduled to meet Friday to choose a successor to Caballero.
